Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires and the players are back on the field and it will be Kushal Bhurtel to open the innings alongside Aasif Sheikh for Nepal. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Right then, India will feel they have one foot in the semifinals already given the score they have posted but Nepal will certainly look to have their say. Will we see Nepal pull off a miracle here? We shall find out as the run chase isn't far away.

Nepal will be a bit disappointed with that bowling effort as they conceded way too many runs in the Powerplay and were unable to take the first wicket for too long. Once they did get a wicket though, the spinners managed to work their magic a bit and kept on picking up regular wickets. Sompal Kami bowled pretty well but did go for a few runs but it was Dipendra Singh Airee who was the pick of the bowlers and picked up two wickets as well. The pacers though, were really expensive and star bowler Abinash Bohara was simply hammered all over the park. They now have a very difficult task ahead.

What a way to end the innings and India have posted a mammoth total on a wicket that isn't batting friendly. India will be considerably happy with that score. Overall, India were a bit patchy with their batting but thankfully for them, Yashasvi Jaiswal  played a blinder of a knock as he smashed the bowlers to all ends of the ground. Jaiswal notched up a sensational hundred as the batters at the other end found it difficult to get going. However, the duo of Shivam Dube and Rinku Singh managed to finish things off with a flourish with the latter really coming into his own in that final over.

Slower length ball outside off. Rinku Singh drags it from outside off and lifts it toward the long-on region. Dipendra Singh Airee stationed there makes a fine effort to time his jump and throw the ball back into play.  He saves four runs for his side. The batters pick up two and India finishes on a formidable 202 for 4.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on leg stump, shaping in a bit, Yashasvi Jaiswal gets it off the toe end of the bat toward short fine leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Muscled away! Fraction short around off hurrying onto the batter. Yashasvi Jaiswal goes for the pull and manages to just clear the square leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Length ball around middle and this one skids on. Ruturaj Gaikwad with an uncharacteristic heave toward the on side but gets hurried on and gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal for LBW but it is turned down and the batters get a leg bye as the ball rolls onto the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Streaky but will do. Good length around off, Ruturaj Gaikwad advances and looks to go over covers but the ball flies off the outer half down to third man for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length on middle and leg, angling in, Yashasvi Jaiswal backs away and nudges it in front of point for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up outside off, Yashasvi Jaiswal drives it on the up to the right of mid off and gets across quickly for the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Karan KC to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Another one! Karan KC overcompensates and bowls it short over leg stump. Yashasvi Jaiswal picks it early again and pulls it over the square leg fence for a biggie. India shifting gears quickly now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Karan KC to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Full and straight, Yashasvi Jaiswal picks the length early and whips it away over wide long on for a maximum, the first of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Karan KC to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: A touch fuller and outside off, eased away with an open bat face to third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Karan KC to Ruturaj Gaikwad, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Half an appeal for LBW but turned down. Length again, slanting in from middle and leg. Ruturaj Gaikwad looks to flick but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Karan KC to Ruturaj Gaikwad, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, right around the top of off, Yashasvi Jaiswal plays it late and just dabs it in front of backward point for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Karan KC to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Karan KC will share the attack from the opposite end.
Full and outside off, shaping away nicely, Ruturaj Gaikwad plays a loose cover drive away from his body and is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the length hard and bowls it at the body, Yashasvi Jaiswal manages to fend it away toward square leg and scampers through for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length ball on the pads and swinging in, Yashasvi Jaiswal tucks it away neatly in front of deep backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up right on the pads, Ruturaj Gaikwad looks to flick it away but mistimes it uppishly to the right of mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A touch fuller again, around off and this one swings away nicely. Ruturaj Gaikwad watches it well and leaves it alone for the keeper to collect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! Very full and close to the off stump, zipping through as well and Ruturaj Gaikwad makes a very well-judged leave.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Sompal Kami to Ruturaj Gaikwad, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Starts with a loosener! Fuller in length, swinging down the leg side and a wide is called. The keeper fumbles and the batters manage to sneak in a run as well. India are up and running.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Sompal Kami to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time for the play to begin! The players and umpires are out in the middle. Ruturaj Gaikwad and Yashasvi Jaiswal will open for India while Sompal Kami will begin the proceedings with the ball for Nepal. Let's go...

Just a few minutes away now from the start but first, the two teams line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Nepal first, followed by the Indian national anthem.
Nepal (Playing XI) - Kushal Bhurtel, Aasif Sheikh (WK), Sundeep Jora, Gulsan Jha, Rohit Paudel (C), Kushal Malla, Dipendra Singh Airee, Sompal Kami, Karan KC, Abinash Bohara, and Sandeep Lamichhane.

India (Playing XI) - Ruturaj Gaikwad (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Tilak Varma, Jitesh Sharma (On debut) (WK), Rinku Singh, Sai Kishore (On debut), Shivam Dube, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Avesh Khan, and Arshdeep Singh.
TOSS - India have won the toss and will BAT first.

Nepal come into this big clash on the back of some impressive performances, none so bigger than the demolition of Mongolia where they became the first Men's team to score 300 plus in T20Is and will hope to put up a real fight here. Can the minnows defeat the giants of Asian Cricket? Or will India cruise through to the semifinals? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

With the ICC Cricket World Cup on the horizon, India have sent what we can call a 'reserve team' just like the other big nations to Hangzhou but it is still a very competitive T20 side with all players having loads of experience thanks to the Indian T20 League. Ruturaj Gaikwad will be looking to lead his side to glory and clinch the Gold medal but first they will need to make a strong start here.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one and all! We are at the ZJUT Cricket Field for the 1st Quarterfinal of the Men's Cricket Competition at the 19th Asian Games and it will be India taking on Nepal for a place in the semifinals.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 19th edition of the Asian Games are in full swing, and things are about to go up a notch in Hangzhou as we approach the quarter-final stage of Men's Cricket event. It all kicks off with India taking on Nepal in the 1st Quarter Final at the ZJUT Cricket Field. Indian women have already clinched a historic gold in the sport, and the Men in Blue will be eager to set out on a journey of their own to go all the way. In their maiden Asian Games appearance, India will be led by talented right-handed batter Ruturaj Gaikwad. He, Yashasvi Jaiswal, and Tilak Varma will form the crux of the Indian top order. The ever-reliable Rinku Singh was impressive during India's tour of Ireland, and he will be eager to stamp his authority in the middle order. Options galore in the all-rounder department, with the presence of Deepak Hooda, Shahbaz Ahmed and Shivam Dube. When it comes to the wicket-keeping duties, the team management has an interesting conundrum with Jitesh Sharma and Prabhsimran Singh jostling for the spot. Keeping in mind their experience for the national side, Washington Sundar and Ravi Bishnoi are likely to get the nod amongst the spin bowling options. The pace attack will be led by left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh and will be accompanied by the likes of Avesh Khan and Mukesh Kumar. On the other hand, Nepal are riding high on confidence after cruising past comparatively lower-ranked sides in the group stage. Their most clinical performance in this year's Asian Games came in their opening encounter against Mongolia, where they rewrote the history books. Rohit Paudel's men now face their first big test against a stronger Indian side. Kushal Malla and Rohit Paudel have done the bulk of the scoring for Nepal, while the likes of Kushal Bhurtel, Aasif Sheikh, and Dipendra Singh Airee have not done badly either. If Nepal are to pose a strong challenge to India, the batting will have to click collectively. With the ball, right-arm seamer Abinash Bohara has single-handedly done the damage for Nepal. The likes of Sandeep Lamichhane, Sompal Kami, and Gulsan Jha have underperformed a bit in terms of wickets and will have to come to the party in this knockout game. The only meeting between these two sides in international cricket came in the recently concluded Asia Cup, where India registered a comprehensive victory. With this being a second-string Indian squad, a potentially tightly-fought contest is on the cards. Will India reign supreme? Or will Nepal manage to spring a surprise? We will find out together.
